workloads:
# Decision packets

For each independent workload improve total output throughput and full-response P90 interactivity. Track P90 TTFT and preserve native quality. Only descendants of the supplied serving image are allowed; keep model, precision, GPU count, client concurrency, trace corpus and quality protocol. Treat each packet as independent. Historical evidence is limited to the supplied index and case cards. The numeric cases are anonymized native observations; packet E is a labeled planning stress test. The device allocation in each packet is its total budget for simultaneous measurement.

## A
An existing one-node serving baseline uses four MI355X, TP4/EP1, external C1, server admission one, five speculative tokens, synthetic acceptance 3.51 for performance. Native output is 135.28933 tok/s, full-response P90 is 418.03893 tok/s/user. The original Docker serves the ordinary path. A source-qualified optional persistent decoder in the same pinned implementation covers the target and this draft at the current width; it needs extra storage. No paired result is available in the packet.

## B
An existing native one-hour baseline serves C64 on two MI355X, TP2/EP1 and DP attention, no host KV. Ordinary target/verify, mixed long prefill and decode on the same devices. Both ranks' periodic samples clipped to native send time:
- dp0/tp0: 2119 periodic decode samples, median active requests 15, observed width p90 21, queued 800/2119, maximum reported token usage 0.26.
- dp1/tp1: 2130 periodic decode samples, median active requests 16.0, observed width p90 22, queued 802/2130, maximum reported token usage 0.16.
Throughput 2424.93493 tok/s, full-response P90 63.24012, TTFT p90 2.6019 s. No operator timings or individual slow-request mapping are supplied. An index scorer consumes per-request KV pages and query rows. The source has separate writers and readers. The cost of their intermediate representations has not yet been measured.

## C
One-node baseline on eight MI355X with external C256, TP8/EP8, DP attention and host KV. Across eight emitting lanes the median number of active requests ranges [16.0, 21.0] and the fraction of decode samples with a queue ranges [0.716, 0.994]. Maximum reported full-token use per lane ranges [0.28, 0.39]. P90 TTFT is 41.63011 s. The archive has no per-rank critical-path trace or fetch/recompute attribution for this packet. Ranks share collective work.

## D
A new workload is supplied as a fixed Docker and CI launch. The requested metrics and parent image are known. No qualified serving baseline, trace or compatible prior is available. Its configured sequence includes a Roofline estimate. One exclusive serving node is available, with some remaining time after a first evaluation.

## E (synthetic stress test)
A serving trace at external C64 has a hard admission cap of one on a single worker. Every completed decode is B1; the queue is growing and TTFT has worsened. No interval trace yet separates time waiting for admission from time executing the decoder. A compatible narrow-step implementation is available. The quality and two primary objectives are unchanged.

base.answer:
## A

**Next module:** Native serving comparison, sequentially on the four-GPU node.

**Question/test:** Does the source-qualified persistent decoder improve both primary metrics versus the ordinary path? Preserve the supplied-image lineage, C1, admission one and five-token speculation. Resolve storage requirements within authorized resources; verify target/draft activation and native quality.

**Tradeoff:** Extra storage may alter memory headroom; synthetic acceptance is not quality evidence.

**Plan-changing report:** Paired throughput, full-response P90, TTFT, activation/storage evidence and observed costs. Native-qualified joint gains support adoption and further search; regressions retain the reference. Activation or storage failures require bounded repair, not dismissal of the opportunity.

## B

**Next module:** Bounded Profile on both ranks, reusing the native C64 baseline.

**Question/test:** At observed decode widths, do scorer intermediates or prefill interruptions dominate serving cost? Attribute writer–reader materialization and scorer execution; align prefill/decode intervals with slow requests. Queue counts and token-use maxima do not establish KV saturation.

**Tradeoff:** Chain fusion requires format compatibility and complete writer/cache validation; admission changes may help interactivity while hurting TTFT.

**Plan-changing report:** Phase/operator costs, request coverage, slow-request attribution and profiling overhead. Dominant intermediate costs prioritize a scoped chain candidate; dominant interruptions prioritize scheduling comparison. Missing attribution remains unresolved, not a negative result.

## C

**Next module:** Coordinated Profile across all eight lanes.

**Question/test:** Which shared critical path drives queues and TTFT: collective stalls, prefill scheduling, or host-KV fetch/recompute? Collect synchronized rank/phase attribution and prefix-chain reuse under representative pressure. Do not infer idle capacity or a cache bottleneck from token-use maxima.

**Tradeoff:** Prefix-preserving eviction needs demonstrated reuse and pressure; scheduling can exchange decode interactivity for TTFT. Rank-local optimization may leave collective waiting unchanged.

**Plan-changing report:** Critical-path attribution, fetch/recompute and usable-prefix evidence, coverage and costs. These select the implicated system/operator route; insufficient representative pressure warrants bounded continuation, not dismissal of host-KV work.

## D

**Next module:** Native baseline evaluation through the fixed Docker/CI launch.

**Question/test:** Can this parent produce a quality-qualified reference for throughput, full-response P90 and TTFT under the declared protocol? Preserve inputs and native receipts; collect a trace if supported, without making optional diagnostics an acceptance gate.

**Tradeoff:** The exclusive node makes investigations compete with evaluation time; Roofline estimates prioritize work but cannot establish serving gains.

**Plan-changing report:** Qualification, launch defects, available trace and actual costs/remaining allowance. Success continues the configured sequence, including Roofline and useful follow-on work; failure triggers bounded repair by the affected owner, preserving partial evidence.

## E

**Next module:** Bounded Profile with an admission discriminator.

**Question/test:** Does cap-one serialization or decoder execution dominate? Separate admission waiting from execution; if permitted and natively supported, perturb admission without changing external C64 or other fixed controls, recording resulting widths.

**Tradeoff:** More admission may improve queueing but alter batching efficiency; narrow-step acceleration preserves serialization. Observed B1 does not establish inherently low demand.

**Plan-changing report:** Timing attribution, cap adjustability and matched primary metrics, TTFT and native quality for any serving probe. Cap-sensitive gains prioritize admission tuning; an immutable cap or dominant execution cost prioritizes narrow-step comparison. Missing intervals remain unknown.

first_draft.answer:
### A
**Next module:** Apply, then Evaluate sequentially on the four-GPU node, retaining the ordinary image as reference. **Question:** Can the source-qualified persistent target/draft decoder improve both serving objectives at fixed C1, admission one and five speculative tokens? Materialize only a pinned-image descendant; test actual route coverage, native quality, throughput, full-response P90, TTFT and KV capacity. **Tradeoff:** Potential narrow-step savings versus extra storage and lost capacity; synthetic acceptance is not quality evidence. Activation/correctness failures prompt bounded repair. A valid paired native report determines adoption and whether further persistent search or profiling remaining serving work earns the next budget.

### B
**Next module:** Profile the baseline on both allocated GPUs. **Question:** Which exposed operators, indexer intermediates or prefill interruptions drive throughput and slow full responses at observed per-rank widths? Test phase/operator timing, slow-request attribution and writer/reader representation costs. Treat fused-indexer-dependency as a compatibility warning, not a predicted gain. **Tradeoff:** Fusion versus scheduling changes, including format/KV-capacity risks and TTFT regressions. The report’s phase/shape attribution selects compatible whole-chain UT, including cache-write correctness, if intermediates matter; UT/Optimize within the allocation for other hotspots; or scheduling comparison for dominant prefill interruption. Adoption requires native quality and serving evidence; queue/token-use statistics alone cannot establish causality.

### C
**Next module:** Profile all eight ranks together, reusing the baseline. **Question:** Is the critical path admission/prefill scheduling, host-KV fetch/recompute, or rank/collective imbalance? Test synchronized per-rank timelines, queue waiting and slow-request attribution; determine whether the unchanged corpus reaches representative cache-chain reuse/eviction pressure. The prefix-chain-LRU case suggests a discriminator, not an established defect. **Tradeoff:** Scheduling/KV/partition changes may reduce TTFT while harming decode interactivity, throughput or collective balance. The attributed report selects a scoped, quality-gated system comparison; exposed operator work instead leads to UT/Optimize. Low token-use statistics alone prove neither compute headroom nor absence of cache pressure.

### D
**Next module:** Baseline using the supplied Docker and CI launch on the exclusive node. **Question:** Can the unchanged stack establish a qualified native reference for throughput, full-response P90 and TTFT? Test the supplied workload and quality protocol; preserve receipts, recovery artifacts and observed costs. Retain the configured Profile, Roofline, UT, Optimize, Apply and Evaluate route. **Tradeoff:** Preparation/validation versus useful search and delivery on one node; keep unknown costs explicit. Baseline failure prompts bounded repair; its valid report establishes the reference and informs budgeting. After the first evaluation, use remaining time to re-profile the best verified descendant or continue useful unresolved search.

### E
**Next module:** Profile the unchanged single-worker route. **Question:** How much TTFT and throughput loss comes from admission waiting versus decoder execution under the cap of one? Test request admission/queue intervals and decode timelines; external C64 does not establish wide execution, nor B1 the bottleneck. **Tradeoff:** Wider admission may reduce waiting but worsen full-response interactivity; narrow-step savings do not remove the cap. The report selects a scoped admission comparison if waiting dominates, or a native-quality-gated narrow-step comparison at fixed admission if decoder cost merits it. Measure both objectives and TTFT; mixed evidence warrants isolated comparisons, not bundled claims.

revised.answer:
All plans preserve fixed inputs, the supplied image reference and resource limits. Adoption requires native quality and serving evidence; P90 TTFT remains tracked.

## A

**Next module: Evaluate.** Can the source-qualified persistent decoder improve throughput and full-response P90 at admission one? Compare ordinary/persistent routes in a supplied-image descendant with identical inputs, five speculative tokens and performance acceptance 3.51. Confirm target/draft activation, native quality, P90 TTFT, storage requirements and actual KV capacity; synthetic acceptance is not quality evidence. Trade reduced narrow-step overhead against extra memory and delivery cost. A valid paired report showing both serving gains supports adoption; memory or TTFT penalties change priorities. Missing qualification or execution failure triggers bounded repair, not a claim that the opportunity is absent.

## B

**Next module: Profile.** Do prefill interruptions, exposed operators, or scorer intermediates limit serving? Measure phase/rank costs, slow-request coverage, intermediate traffic and writer/reader format dependencies at observed widths. Fused-indexer history motivates checking the complete compatible chain, not assuming transfer. If independently qualifiable, attention/index-scoring and GEMM UTs can run on separate single-GPU slots; TP2 comparisons reserve both GPUs. Fusion must beat the best compatible unfused chain, including writers. Trade kernel/fusion delivery cost against scheduling gains and TTFT risk. The report’s exposed-cost attribution selects UT, fusion investigation, or an admission/prefill-interval comparison.

## C

**Next module: Profile.** Which stage sets the eight-GPU critical path: admission, host-KV fetch/recompute, attention/expert work, or collective waiting? Trace all lanes together and attribute TTFT and slow-response stalls; inspect prefix-chain availability under representative reuse and capacity pressure. Reported token usage does not prove spare effective capacity. Trade scheduling/KV changes against kernel search and their serving effects. Independently qualifiable attention/KV and expert-GEMM UTs could use separate single-GPU slots; shared collectives and serving reserve eight GPUs. A report showing lost usable prefixes prioritizes a KV-policy probe; rank imbalance prioritizes partitioning; exposed operators prioritize UT.

## D

**Next module: Baseline.** Can the supplied Docker/CI launch produce a native-quality-qualified serving reference for all three metrics? Preserve the parent image, inputs and recovery artifacts; investigate launch or qualification defects within this call. Continue Baseline→Profile→UT→Optimize→Apply→Evaluate, retaining Roofline in its configured position. Profile could dispatch independent attention/KV and GEMM UTs on disjoint devices where qualified; serving comparisons reserve the node. Trade search depth against preparation, cold checks and delivery costs. A valid baseline report opens profiling; failures return to their owner. After evaluation, use remaining time to re-profile or continue promising unresolved search.

## E

**Next module: Profile.** At fixed admission one, what portion of delay is admission waiting versus decoder and other occupied-worker work? Collect interval traces of queueing, service time and launch/synchronization costs. B1 completions alone do not identify the bottleneck. Use the sole worker; subsequent narrow-step UT and serving comparisons need separate measurement windows. Trade faster single-request service against admission/scheduling constraints and implementation cost. A report showing exposed decoder overhead prioritizes qualification and a fixed-cap ordinary/narrow comparison; admission stalls with little decoder headroom prioritize a permitted scheduling probe. Queue-heavy TTFT alone does not rule out decoder acceleration.

independent_kimi_plan:
Pin parent, workload, seeds, quality criteria, protocol and metric definitions in BRIEF.md. Profile parent, then run matched-state, reference-length A/B and B/A comparisons of prefill_decode_interval=16 versus 8, holding admission=32, draft=6, TP8/EP1 and KV capacity fixed. Bound this checkpoint to one toggle; record preparation, execution, validation and waits.

Measure per-worker active requests/token rows, phase/operator costs, rank stalls and queue delay. Observed widths 15/23 favor wide-path investigation, not C1 monokernel extrapolation. Test whether more frequent prefill reduces waiting or steals decode/verify capacity; queueing and KV=0.49 do not establish admission/capacity causality.

Serving needs exclusive eight-GPU windows. If compute dominates, qualify attention/KV and GEMM/routing rank-local UTs concurrently, one disjoint GPU each; collectives need eight GPUs separately. Regional fusion must beat the best compatible unfused operators.

Adopt only on native Evaluate evidence of preserved quality and repeatable improvements in output throughput and P90 full-response speed. Report TTFT versus 4.69676s and queue delay. Otherwise retain parent; returned costs/coverage rerank the next call.
